name: equal_effort_baseline_slowed
description: PLACEHOLDER -- NOT RUNNABLE AS SHIPPED. The equal-effort question from the other direction: instead of speeding DeepSetsBotExp up until it evaluates as many positions per turn as the baseline, slow SakkirinaScaled down until it evaluates as few as DeepSetsBotExp. Same question, same target ratio, opposite side moved. Fill in the one TBD from a calibration run before submitting anything.
_why_two_directions: equal_effort.json and this config answer the same question by moving opposite sides, and
BOTH are run because neither is decisive on its own.
Speeding the treatment up (equal_effort.json) keeps the baseline at exactly the timing it
competes at, which is the timing its author tuned it for. The cost is that it hands
DeepSetsBotExp a per-turn budget no tournament would ever give it -- around 78s -- so the
agent being measured is not the agent that was submitted, and the run costs roughly 8x the
wall clock of every other experiment.
Slowing the baseline down (this config) keeps DeepSetsBotExp at exactly the timing it
competes at, and costs no more than a normal row. The cost is that it runs SakkirinaSolo's
search at about an eighth of the budget it was designed around, and a hand-tuned heuristic
agent may degrade non-linearly there -- its rule-based fast paths and tree reuse do not
scale with the clock, so the shape of its play changes, not just its depth.
So each direction has a distortion the other does not, and the distortions are not the same
kind. What carries weight is AGREEMENT: if both directions move the win rate the same way,
the conclusion is robust to which side was moved and neither distortion explains it. If they
disagree, that is the interesting result -- it means evaluations per turn is not the right
currency for 'effort' in this matchup, and the equal-effort framing itself needs rethinking
before either number is reported.
Run this one first. It is cheap, and if it already answers the question the expensive
direction becomes a confirmation rather than the primary evidence.
_how_to_fill_this_in: ONE calibration run serves BOTH equal-effort configs -- it measures the ratio, and the two
configs just apply it to opposite sides. Either config's --calibrate produces it:
1. Read the measured ratio r = SakkirinaScaled evals/turn / DeepSetsBotExp evals/turn.
The local pilot gave r ~ 8.1 (see _calibration_so_far below).
2. Set matchups[0].env.SOT_BASELINE_TIME_SCALE = 1/r. At r = 8.1 that is about 0.12.
NOTE the harness prints SUGGESTED SOT_TIME_SCALE, which is r itself -- the number for
THIS config is its RECIPROCAL, because here the baseline's clock moves, not ours.
3. timeout stays 12: both sides have a bot-side cap of at most 9.8s (DeepSetsBotExp is at
scale 1.0 and the baseline is slower still), so the normal margin is enough. This is the
whole reason this direction is cheap.
4. Re-run --calibrate against the filled-in values to confirm the two evals/turn figures
actually meet, then submit the 400-game array.
The harness REFUSES to run any matchup whose timeout or env still says TBD.
_calibration_so_far: Local pilot, 2026-09-22, 10 games, SOT_ALPHA0=0, both sides at scale 1.0, --timeout 12.
NOT a substitute for a cluster run -- different hardware, and n=10 is not enough.
DeepSetsBotExp   9459 evals/turn pooled  (106,891 /game, sd 3825 across games)
SakkirinaScaled 76699 evals/turn pooled  (905,048 /game, sd 31776 across games)
ratio r = 8.11x per turn pooled, 8.47x per game pooled
per-game ratio ranged 2.71x .. 21.07x; 95% CI on the mean [5.65, 13.03]
CORRECTION 2026-09-23: an earlier version of this note said a run at SOT_ALPHA0=0.7 gave
14.95x, and attributed the gap to the blend running both evaluators. That was wrong -- it
compared an n=2 run against this n=10 one, and the per-game ratio spans 2.71x..21.07x, so
the difference was sampling noise. A paired measurement over 6 seeds puts the blend's
throughput cost at ~1.6%. alpha0=0 is still pinned here, for the plain reason: this
experiment is about the NETWORK as an evaluator, so calibrate on the agent you will run.
The CI is wide enough that r should be re-derived from >=20 cluster games.

matchups.label: equal_effort_baseline_slowed
matchups.note: DeepSetsBotExp is the fixed point here: SOT_TIME_SCALE=1.0 is exactly the timing it competes at, and SOT_ALPHA0=0 makes it the pure-network agent (behaviourally DeepSetsBot). Only the baseline's clock moves. Expected SOT_BASELINE_TIME_SCALE around 0.12; it must come from a calibration run, not from this note.

matchups.label: calibrate_stock_speed
matchups.note: Identical to equal_effort.json's calibration block on purpose -- one measurement, both directions. Both sides at scale 1.0 measures the ratio at stock timing; the two configs then apply it to opposite sides. SakkirinaScaled rather than SakkirinaSolo because stock SakkirinaSolo emits no throughput telemetry, and at scale 1.0 the two are timing-identical.
